az_uptown.blurb: Uptown is the northern half of West Elden, an old-school dacite cliff on the lower flank of Mount Elden just north of Flagstaff. A fence splits the cliff, with Downtown on the far side. The rock is rough and grippy, the walls top out around 80 feet, and nearly everything here is traditional: cracks, slabs and faces. Of the 22 climbs, 20 are trad, with a single sport route and a single top rope. Grades start at 5.4 and reach 5.12, but most land between 5.9 and 5.11. Sitting near 7,700 feet, it works as a summer escape from the heat, with shade in the morning and sun later in the day. The walk from the car is mild.

az_davidson_wall.blurb: Davidson Wall is one of the tallest faces at Paradise Forks, a columnar basalt canyon in the Kaibab National Forest about half an hour west of Flagstaff, at roughly 7,000 feet. It faces west, so summer mornings are shaded and the rest of the day is sunny. All 22 routes are traditional, mostly steep, long crack lines, and the wall is known for hard crack classics. Grades begin at 5.9, with the bulk between 5.10 and 5.12 and one 5.13; expect stout ratings. Climbs are usually reached by fixing a line and rappelling in from the rim.

az_thirteen_mile_rock.blurb: Thirteen Mile Rock is a small basalt butte beside Highway 260, east of I-17, in the central Mogollon Rim country of northern Arizona. It is a small, mostly bolted crag: of the 22 climbs, 19 are sport and 3 are trad. Grades run from about 5.6 to 5.10, with the largest group at 5.10 and plenty at 5.8, so it suits climbers at moderate and low-intermediate levels. Lines on the butte's faces are described as steep, and at least one is around 90 feet with easy ground until a harder finish. Anchors are bolted, with chains on some routes. Few details are published about the approach or the season, so scout conditions before driving out.

az_main_wall_south.blurb: This is the southern end of the Main Wall in Isolation Canyon, a quartzite crag in the Tonto National Forest just outside Pine, in central Arizona. It covers the routes beyond the fixed-line traverse, and the wall faces east. Climbing here is a mix of sport and trad: of 22 climbs, 12 are sport, 9 are trad and one is a top rope. Grades run from 5.8 to 5.11, with most at 5.10 and 5.11, so it favors confident intermediates over beginners. To reach the far routes you duck under a low roof while following the fixed line. Several of the better lines pick up three-and-a-half to four star ratings from climbers.

az_weathertop.blurb: Weathertop is a west-facing cliff on Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains near Tucson, in the lowest stretch of the Catalina Highway, and you can spot it from the road. It is the biggest cliff in that section, consistently over 100 feet tall. Of its 21 climbs, 12 are trad and 9 are sport. Grades run from 5.8 to 5.12, with nearly half at 5.11, so it leans toward stronger climbers. The setting is Sonoran Desert with saguaros, and the lower highway is recommended in the winter months. Rock quality is average for low mountain stone. Expect a real uphill hike to the ridge, and descend by rappelling or walking off the north side.

az_sunshine_boulder.blurb: Sunshine Boulder is part of the main bouldering area at Beardsley, a pile of coarse, weathered desert granite on the north edge of Phoenix, visible from the 101 freeway. It holds 21 problems spread from VB up to V7, with a few at nearly every level, so a mixed group can find something. Grades here are old-school and can feel stiff, and problems reach about 15 feet, so bring a pad. Park at the small dead-end lot, then walk roughly a third of a mile northwest to the main area.
az_sunshine_boulder.parking_note: Park in the small dead-end lot at the end of Lone Cactus Road. From the junction of the 101 and Cave Creek Road, head north on Cave Creek for about half a mile, then turn left onto Lone Cactus Road.

az_stewart_peak.blurb: Stewart Peak is a cone-shaped granite dome, roughly 150 to 200 feet high, in Stewart Pocket, a lightly developed climbing area near Payson in central Arizona. The rock is mostly good and the views are nice. Climbs are a blend of trad and sport, with some lines done either way and some running to several pitches. Of 21 climbs, 14 are trad and 7 are sport. Grades start with one very easy line and mostly sit between 5.8 and 5.10, with a couple of 5.11s, which makes it a friendly choice for moderate climbers. You hike in on a trail from a gate; stay on the path as much as possible, and expect a faint climbers' trail near the base.
az_stewart_peak.parking_note: Turn onto Granite Dells Road just off Highway 260 in Payson. The pavement soon turns to dirt, and the road ends at a closed gate near a big wash. Park in the pullout nearby and continue on foot.
